exposure: mode of delivery (Caesarean section vs vaginal delivery)
cohort: 1019 term deliveries of women participating in the prospective Health and Early Life Microbiota (HELMi) birth cohort study between March 2016 and March 2018 in the capital region of Finland
finding: The study found that over one-third of mothers received antibiotics during childbirth, and this was associated with increased defecation frequency in infants during the first months and higher weight gain at three months of age.
mod_finding: Antibiotic use was significantly higher in caesarean sections (100%) compared to vaginal deliveries (37%).
